claim: WbaP is a phosphoglycosyl transferase from the Salmonella enterica (LT2) O-antigen biosynthesis.

evidence: This is supported by established knowledge and citations in the manuscript.

claim: WbaP is a homodimer.
source: From a functional perspective, these studies establish WbaP as a homodimer, reveal the structural elements responsible for dimerization, shed light on the regulatory role of a domain of unknown function embedded within WbaP, and identify conserved structural motifs between PGTs and functionally unrelated UDP-sugar dehydratases.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including crosslinking, mass spectrometry, and CryoEM.

claim: The logic of the Wzx/Wzy-dependent glycoconjugate biosynthesis pathways is highly conserved.
source: The logic of the Wzx/Wzy-dependent glycoconjugate biosynthesis pathways is highly conserved and comprises a series of enzyme-catalyzed transfer reactions using nucleoside diphosphate sugar donor substrates and a membrane resident polyprenol phosphate (PrenP) acceptor such as undecaprenol phosphate (UndP).
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: WbaP catalyzes the transfer of phospho-galactose from UDP-galactose to UndP, forming Und-PP-galactose.

claim: The β-hairpin domain swap within a homodimer is highly conserved among Lg-PGTs.
source: Significantly, the prediction of structures of other Lg-PGTs reveals that this β-hairpin domain swap within a homodimer is highly conserved (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on analysis of AlphaFold predictions of other Lg-PGTs.

claim: Concentration-dependent crosslinking was observed for two discrete sets of crosslinking pairs along the predicted domain swap interface using either Cu phenanthroline or bBBr.
source: We observed concentration-dependent crosslinking for two discrete sets of crosslinking pairs along the predicted domain swap interface using either Cu phenanthroline or bBBr (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from targeted crosslinking experiments.

claim: No crosslinking was observed for wild-type WbaP using either Cu phenanthroline or bBBr crosslinking strategies.
source: No crosslinking was observed for wild-type protein using either crosslinking strategy, demonstrating that there are no native cysteines within crosslinking distance, (Figure 5E) as predicted by the AlphaFold dimer model.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from targeted crosslinking experiments.

claim: In-solution digestion of crosslinked WbaP resulted in fragments covering 93.86% of S. enterica WbaP.
source: In-solution digestion resulted in fragments covering 93.86% S. enterica WbaP, and 49 unique crosslinking sites were identified (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from crosslinking mass spectrometry.

claim: 49 unique crosslinking sites were identified in crosslinked WbaP.
source: In-solution digestion resulted in fragments covering 93.86% S. enterica WbaP, and 49 unique crosslinking sites were identified (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from crosslinking mass spectrometry.

claim: The majority of the DSS crosslinks localized to the solvent-accessible areas of the PGT domain.
source: The majority of the DSS crosslinks localized to the solvent-accessible areas of the PGT domain, while several of the tBu-PhoX crosslinks localized to the membrane-adjacent regions at the putative dimer interface (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from crosslinking mass spectrometry.

claim: Several of the tBu-PhoX crosslinks localized to the membrane-adjacent regions at the putative dimer interface.
source: The majority of the DSS crosslinks localized to the solvent-accessible areas of the PGT domain, while several of the tBu-PhoX crosslinks localized to the membrane-adjacent regions at the putative dimer interface (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from crosslinking mass spectrometry.

claim: The observed inter-chain crosslinks agreed with the predicted dimer interface.
source: The observed inter-chain crosslinks agreed with the predicted dimer interface, with Lys273 proximal to Lys146, Lys148, and Lys81. In addition, Lys81 and Lys451 were within crosslinking range (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from crosslinking mass spectrometry and comparison to the AlphaFold model.

claim: A moderate-resolution (~4.1 Å by GSFSC) CryoEM reconstruction of WbaP was obtained from 196,663 particles.
source: Subsequent masked refinement and cleaning of particle stacks led to a moderate-resolution (~4.1 Å by GSFSC) reconstruction from 196,663 particles which was consistent with the AlphaFold model (Figure 7A and B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from CryoEM.

claim: The CryoEM reconstruction of WbaP was consistent with the AlphaFold model.
source: Subsequent masked refinement and cleaning of particle stacks led to a moderate-resolution (~4.1 Å by GSFSC) reconstruction from 196,663 particles which was consistent with the AlphaFold model (Figure 7A and B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from CryoEM and comparison to the AlphaFold model.

claim: Docking and real-space refinement led to the placement of 796 out of 1056 residues of the WbaP dimer.
source: Docking and real-space refinement led to the placement of 796 out of 1056 residues of the dimer (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from CryoEM and structural modeling.

claim: Superposition between the refined CryoEM model and the AlphaFold dimer prediction results in an RMSD of 2.83 Å.
source: Superposition between the refined model and the AlphaFold dimer prediction results in an RMSD of 2.83 Å, demonstrating close agreement between the two models (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the CryoEM model and the AlphaFold prediction.

claim: The overall architecture of the WbaP dimer is T-shaped.
source: The overall architecture of the WbaP dimer is T-shaped, with the two four-TMH bundles forming the central stalk, each capped by a DUF.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure.

claim: The dimer interface of WbaP comprises ~780 Å2 of buried surface area, involving 7.1% of the residues of the protein.
source: The dimer interface comprises ~780 Å2 of buried surface area, involving 7.1% of the residues of the protein.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure.

claim: A modest (176 Å2) interface is found along the four TMH bundles of WbaP, with the C-terminal half of helix 3 (Ile99 – Phe107) mediating contacts.
source: A modest (176 Å2) interface is found along the four TMH bundles, with the C-terminal half of helix 3 (Ile99 – Phe107) mediating contacts.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure.

claim: The N-termini of helix 3 in the WbaP dimer (Pro82) are ~32 Å apart, creating a large void in the center of the dimer, which is presumably occupied by phospholipid.
source: While the C-terminal regions of helix 3 are within interacting distance, the N-termini (Pro82) are ~32 Å apart, creating a large void in the center of the dimer, which is presumably occupied by phospholipid.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure and inference about the contents of the void.

claim: The remainder of the dimer interface of WbaP occurs at the DUF domains, mediated almost entirely by the β-hairpin domain crossover.
source: The remainder of the dimer interface occurs at the DUF domains, mediated almost entirely by the β-hairpin domain crossover discussed above.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure.

claim: The DUF domains cap the cytosolic loops between the four TMH bundles in WbaP.
source: Based on previous experiments establishing the topology of monoPGT catalytic domains, the DUF domains cap the cytosolic loops between the four TMH bundles (Ray et al., 2018; Furlong et al., 2015; Entova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure and citations to prior research on monoPGT topology.

claim: The catalytic domains of the Lg-PGT WbaP protrude away from the dimer interface, placing the two active sites 77 Å apart.
source: The catalytic domains of the Lg-PGT protrude away from the dimer interface, placing the two active sites 77 Å apart.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure.

claim: The interdigitating β-hairpin motif at the dimer interface between the DUF domains places Ser259 only ~23 Å from the active site of the opposite chain.
source: Despite the large distance between catalytic sites, the interdigitating β-hairpin motif at the dimer interface between the DUF domains places Ser259, found at the apex of the turn of the β-hairpin, only ~23 Å from the active site of the opposite chain.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure and AlphaFold model.

claim: The β-hairpin motif is poorly ordered in the experimental CryoEM map of WbaP.
source: Although the β-hairpin is poorly ordered in the experimental map, the targeted Cys-pair crosslinking confirms the placement of this motif found in the AlphaFold model.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure.

claim: A predicted helix-turn-helix motif from residues 337–369 of the catalytic domain is disordered in the experimental CryoEM map of WbaP.
source: A predicted helix-turn-helix motif from residues 337–369 of the catalytic domain is also disordered in the experimental map (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure.

claim: The helix-turn-helix motif in WbaP is analogous to a mobile loop found in the C. concisus PglC, which has been implicated in the formation of the substrate binding pocket.
source: This region is analogous to a mobile loop found in the C. concisus PglC, which has been implicated in the formation of the substrate binding pocket (Anderson et al., 2023)
evidence: This is based on comparison to prior research on PglC.

claim: The length, sequence conservation, and structural motifs of the region proximal to the active site differ greatly between PglC and WbaP.
source: Although both the mobile loop in PglC and the helix-turn-helix found in WbaP are positioned proximal to the active site, the length, sequence conservation, and structural motifs of this region differ greatly between these two PGTs (Figure 8).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the structures of PglC and WbaP.

claim: Modifications around the conserved catalytic site may provide a structural rationale for the differing UDP-sugar substrate specificities between PglC and WbaP.
source: These modifications around the conserved catalytic site may provide a structural rationale for the differing UDP-sugar substrate specificities between PglC and WbaP.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from the structural differences.

claim: XLMS experiments demonstrate that lysines within the predicted helix-turn-helix of WbaP can crosslink with lysines across the soluble core of the catalytic domain.
source: XLMS experiments demonstrate that lysines within the predicted helix-turn-helix of WbaP can crosslink with lysines across the soluble core of the catalytic domain (Figure 6C), giving high confidence to the placement of this region in the AlphaFold model, despite the lack of density in the experimental map.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from crosslinking mass spectrometry.

claim: A structural description of a WbaP ortholog from E. coli by CryoEM was published during the course of this work.
source: During the course of this work, a structural description of a WbaP ortholog from E. coli (NCBI:taxid562) by CryoEM was published (Uchański et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a citation to prior research.

claim: The E. coli WbaP protein was purified using both detergent and amphipols.
source: This protein was purified using both detergent and amphipols, and was complexed with a nanobody fusion to facilitate particle identification and alignment during 3D-reconstruction.
evidence: This is based on the methods described in the cited publication.

claim: The E. coli WbaP was complexed with a nanobody fusion to facilitate particle identification and alignment during 3D-reconstruction.
source: This protein was purified using both detergent and amphipols, and was complexed with a nanobody fusion to facilitate particle identification and alignment during 3D-reconstruction.
evidence: This is based on the methods described in the cited publication.

claim: Visual comparison between S. enterica WbaP and published images of the E. coli WbaP reveals an overall similar architecture, including disorder in the helix-turn-helix region.
source: Although the maps and models associated with this data are not yet publicly available, visual comparison between S. enterica WbaP and published images of the E. coli WbaP reveals an overall similar architecture, including disorder in the helix-turn-helix region.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the S. enterica WbaP structure to published images of E. coli WbaP.

claim: The handedness of the E. coli WbaP reconstruction is inverted compared to S. enterica WbaP as well as the predicted AlphaFold model.
source: However, the handedness of the E. coli WbaP reconstruction is inverted compared to S. enterica WbaP as well as the predicted AlphaFold model.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the S. enterica WbaP structure to published images of E. coli WbaP.

claim: A construct encoding residues 146–272 of WbaP resulted in the production of soluble protein.
source: A construct encoding residues 146–272 resulted in the production of soluble protein (Figure 9—figure supplement 1), which was then used to screen for potential nucleotide ligands by nano differential scanning fluorimetry (nDSF, Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from protein expression and purification.

claim: The truncated DUF construct (residues 146-272) was used to screen for potential nucleotide ligands by nDSF.
source: A construct encoding residues 146–272 resulted in the production of soluble protein (Figure 9—figure supplement 1), which was then used to screen for potential nucleotide ligands by nano differential scanning fluorimetry (nDSF, Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: The nDSF screen identified UMP, UDP, and UTP as potential stabilizing ligands for the truncated DUF construct.
source: This screen identified UMP, UDP, and UTP as potential stabilizing ligands, and also demonstrated that the UDP-Gal substrate of the catalytic domain destabilized the truncated DUF construct.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from nDSF.

claim: UDP-Gal destabilized the truncated DUF construct.
source: This screen identified UMP, UDP, and UTP as potential stabilizing ligands, and also demonstrated that the UDP-Gal substrate of the catalytic domain destabilized the truncated DUF construct.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from nDSF.

claim: The DUF plays a role in allosteric regulation by sensing nucleotides and nucleotide sugars.
source: These results imply that the DUF plays a role in allosteric regulation by sensing nucleotides and nucleotide sugars.
evidence: This is an inference based on the nDSF and inhibition data.

claim: Full-length WbaP was found to be strongly inhibited by UMP, with an apparent IC50 of 4.1 μM.
source: Indeed, full-length WbaP was found to be strongly inhibited by UMP, with an apparent IC50 of 4.1 μM (Figure 9).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from inhibition assays.

claim: UMP has an apparent Ki of 3 μM for the WbaP ortholog CpsE.
source: This is in close agreement with studies on the WbaP ortholog CpsE, for which UMP has an apparent Ki of 3 μM (Cartee et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The unusual profile of the UMP inhibition curve may reflect UMP binding both competitively to UDP-Gal at the active site, as well as to an allosteric site within the DUF.
source: The unusual profile of the UMP inhibition curve may reflect UMP binding both competitively to UDP-Gal at the active site, as well as to an allosteric site within the DUF.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from the inhibition data.

claim: The DUF may act as a regulatory domain, preventing the overuse of limited UndP resources by modulating PGT activity in response to excess UMP production.
source: Thus, it appears that the DUF may act as a regulatory domain, preventing the overuse of limited UndP resources by modulating PGT activity in response to excess UMP production.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: A search of the PDB for structural homologs of the DUF alone returned only nucleotide-binding domains with limited homology to the DUF.
source: The N-terminal domains found in WbaP are highly conserved across the Lg-PGT family, (O'Toole et al., 2021b) however, a search of the PDB for structural homologs of the domain alone returned only nucleotide-binding domains with limited homology to the DUF.
evidence: This is based on a search of the PDB database.

claim: The N-terminal domains of WbaP exhibited structural homology to models generated from a class of NDP-sugar dehydratases involved in glycoconjugate biosynthesis when analyzed using Foldseek.
source: To sample a larger set of structural models, we utilized the recently described Foldseek tool to parse the AlphaFold model database (AFDB proteome) (van Kempen et al., 2023). In this analysis, although most of the aligned models were other PGTs, the N-terminal domains of WbaP also exhibited structural homology to models generated from a class of NDP-sugar dehydratases involved in glycoconjugate biosynthesis (Figure 10).
evidence: This is based on analysis using Foldseek and the AlphaFold model database.

claim: Homologs identified by Foldseek include PglF from Campylobacter and Cap5D from Staphylococcus.
source: Homologs identified by Foldseek include PglF from Campylobacter and Cap5D from Staphylococcus.
evidence: This is based on analysis using Foldseek.

claim: PglF-like dehydratases are well characterized both structurally and mechanistically.
source: This family of DHs is well characterized both structurally and mechanistically, however, constructs used for most structural studies are truncated at the N-terminus and do not include the transmembrane domain or DUF technical reasons (Riegert et al., 2017; Olivier et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Constructs used for most structural studies of PglF-like dehydratases are truncated at the N-terminus and do not include the transmembrane domain or DUF.
source: This family of DHs is well characterized both structurally and mechanistically, however, constructs used for most structural studies are truncated at the N-terminus and do not include the transmembrane domain or DUF technical reasons (Riegert et al., 2017; Olivier et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The conservation of N-terminal domains between PGTs and PglF-like dehydratases is puzzling, and warrants re-examination of full-length constructs of PglF-like DHs.
source: As these two classes of enzymes are functionally unrelated, the conservation of their N-terminal domains is puzzling, and warrants re-examination of full-length constructs of PglF-like DHs.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the unexpected structural homology.

claim: The strategy applied here will be broadly applicable to other bacterial membrane proteins.
source: We anticipate that the strategy applied here will be broadly applicable to other bacterial membrane proteins and provide an efficient route to map the structure of target proteins in a near-native environment, even in the absence of high-resolution structural data.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential application of the methods.

claim: The methods developed here will be well suited to the study of membrane protein complexes or membrane-bound metabolons.
source: In addition, these methods will be well suited to the study of membrane protein complexes or membrane-bound metabolons, (Møller, 2010; Bassard and Laursen, 2019) a long-standing goal in the study of glycoconjugate biosynthesis.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential application of the methods.

claim: The structure presented represents the first monotopic PGT characterized in the native-like membrane of a liponanoparticle.
source: The structure presented represents the first monotopic PGT characterized in the native-like membrane of a liponanoparticle.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the work.

claim: In contrast to the Sm-PGT PglC from Campylobacter, which is functional as a monomer, the S. enterica Lg-PGT, WbaP, is a tightly associated dimer.
source: We show that in contrast to the Sm-PGT PglC from Campylobacter, which is functional as a monomer, the S. enterica Lg-PGT, WbaP, is a tightly associated dimer, with the majority of inter-chain contacts occurring in the highly conserved but previously uncharacterized DUF.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from this study and citations to prior research on PglC.

claim: The majority of inter-chain contacts in the WbaP dimer occur in the highly conserved but previously uncharacterized DUF.
source: We show that in contrast to the Sm-PGT PglC from Campylobacter, which is functional as a monomer, the S. enterica Lg-PGT, WbaP, is a tightly associated dimer, with the majority of inter-chain contacts occurring in the highly conserved but previously uncharacterized DUF.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from this study.

claim: Thermal denaturation binding experiments implicate the DUF in uridine nucleotide and UDP-sugar binding.
source: Despite computational assignment as a CoA-binding domain, thermal denaturation binding experiments implicate the DUF in uridine nucleotide and UDP-sugar binding.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from nDSF.

claim: Biochemical assays show that UMP is a potent inhibitor of full-length WbaP activity.
source: Biochemical assays show that UMP is a potent inhibitor of full-length WbaP activity (Figure 9).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from inhibition assays.

claim: The profile of the UMP inhibition curve suggests additional UMP interactions beyond the active site in the full-length protein.
source: The profile of the inhibition curve suggests additional UMP interactions beyond the active site in the full-length protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on the shape of the inhibition curve.

claim: The DUF serves both a structural and functional role in stabilizing the dimer and allosterically regulating the catalytic domain upon UMP binding.
source: Taken together, these results point toward the DUF serving both a structural and functional role in stabilizing the dimer and allosterically regulating the catalytic domain upon UMP binding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data.

claim: Allosteric regulation of PGT catalysis via the DUF represents a 'one-size-fits-all' approach to regulating Lg-PGTs with differing NDP-sugar substrates.
source: As UMP is produced by PGTs regardless of the sugar moiety of the NDP-sugar substrate, allosteric regulation of PGT catalysis via the DUF represents a 'one-size-fits-all' approach to regulating Lg-PGTs with differing NDP-sugar substrates.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and knowledge of PGT biochemistry.

claim: DUF-based modulation of PGT function provides a consistent explanation for the in vivo observation that S. pneumoniae CpsE accumulates suppressor mutations within its DUF in a system where PGT activity is lethal.
source: DUF-based modulation of PGT function provides a consistent explanation for the in vivo observation that S. pneumoniae CpsE accumulates suppressor mutations within its DUF in a system where PGT activity is lethal (James et al., 2013; Cartee et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and citations to prior research.

claim: There is a surprising structural homology between the N-terminal domains of Lg-PGTs and PglF-like dehydratases.
source: Intriguingly, we observe a surprising structural homology between the N-terminal domains of Lg-PGTs and PglF-like dehydratases, which are common UDP-sugar modifying enzymes involved in the biogenesis of unusual carbohydrates for glycoconjugate biosynthesis.
evidence: This is based on analysis using Foldseek and the AlphaFold model database.

claim: PglF-like dehydratases are common UDP-sugar modifying enzymes involved in the biogenesis of unusual carbohydrates for glycoconjugate biosynthesis.
source: Intriguingly, we observe a surprising structural homology between the N-terminal domains of Lg-PGTs and PglF-like dehydratases, which are common UDP-sugar modifying enzymes involved in the biogenesis of unusual carbohydrates for glycoconjugate biosynthesis.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: The DUFs may play a larger role in the modulation of the flux of glycoconjugate biosynthesis by subjecting both Lg-PGTs and PglF-like dehydratases to negative feedback by pathway-side products.
source: In this case, it is tempting to hypothesize that the DUFs may play a larger role in the modulation of the flux of glycoconjugate biosynthesis by subjecting both Lg-PGTs and PglF-like dehydratases to negative feedback by pathway-side products.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the structural homology and experimental data.

claim: PglC and WbaP are predicted to catalyze similar chemical transformations.
source: Although PglC and WbaP are predicted to catalyze similar chemical transformations, these PGT enzymes exhibit different substrate specificity.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of PGT biochemistry.

claim: PglC and WbaP exhibit different substrate specificity.
source: Although PglC and WbaP are predicted to catalyze similar chemical transformations, these PGT enzymes exhibit different substrate specificity.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of PGT biochemistry.

claim: PglC shows high specificity for UDP-diNAcBac.
source: PglC shows high specificity for UDP-diNAcBac, while WbaP is specific for UDP-Gal.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of PGT biochemistry.

claim: WbaP is specific for UDP-Gal.
source: PglC shows high specificity for UDP-diNAcBac, while WbaP is specific for UDP-Gal.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of PGT biochemistry.

claim: Structural and sequence elements were identified that facilitated the bioinformatic assignment of substrate specificity to Sm-PGTs that use the same UDP-diNAcBac substrate as PglC.
source: Recently, structural and sequence elements were identified that facilitated the bioinformatic assignment of substrate specificity to Sm-PGTs that use the same UDP-diNAcBac substrate as PglC (Anderson et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The major structural deviations between PglC and WbaP occur in regions important for substrate specificity.
source: Interestingly, the major structural deviations between PglC and WbaP occur in these regions (Figure 8).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the structures of PglC and WbaP.

claim: An extended loop containing a conserved 'GLLP' motif in diNAcBac-utilizing PGTs is replaced with a predicted helix-turn-helix motif in WbaP.
source: An extended loop containing a conserved 'GLLP' motif in diNAcBac-utilizing PGTs is replaced with a predicted helix-turn-helix motif in WbaP.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the structures of PglC and WbaP.

claim: The helix-turn-helix motif in WbaP is poorly resolved in the experimental CryoEM reconstruction.
source: This region is poorly resolved in the experimental CryoEM reconstruction of WbaP, however, lysines in this putative structural motif crosslink with the main domain of the WbaP dimer.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the CryoEM structure.

claim: A mechanism is envisioned in which the active site of WbaP 'closes' upon the helix-turn-helix motion towards the center of the dimer, and the active site is 'open' when the motif moves away.
source: Given the apparent high degree of motion in the vitrified WbaP particles at this region, and the proximity of the helix-turn-helix motif to the active site, we envision a mechanism in which the active site 'closes' upon the helix-turn-helix motion towards the center of the dimer, and the active site is 'open' when the motif moves away, as observed in the AlphaFold model.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from the structural data.

claim: The proposed mechanism for WbaP active site opening and closing resembles structural conformers observed in both crystal structures and molecular dynamics simulations of C. concisus PglC.
source: This resembles structural conformers observed in both crystal structures and molecular dynamics simulations of C. concisus PglC (Majumder et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: An aromatic box motif is predictive of substrate specificity in diNAcBac-specific PGTs.
source: Another structural element in the diNAcBac-specific PGTs that is predictive of substrate specificity is an aromatic box motif comprising residues in the solvent-accessible region of the protein and a conserved Phe near the C-terminus of this subset of Sm-PGTs (Anderson et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In WbaP, the C-terminus of the catalytic domain is ~14 amino acids shorter than in the diNAcBac Sm-PGTs.
source: In WbaP, the C-terminus of the catalytic domain is ~14 amino acids shorter than in the diNAcBac Sm-PGTs, and the aromatic box motif is absent.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the structures of PglC and WbaP.

claim: The aromatic box motif is absent in WbaP.
source: In WbaP, the C-terminus of the catalytic domain is ~14 amino acids shorter than in the diNAcBac Sm-PGTs, and the aromatic box motif is absent.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the structures of PglC and WbaP.

claim: Subtle changes surrounding the conserved Asp-Glu catalytic dyad are likely to drive the specificity of WbaP to UDP-Gal.
source: These subtle changes surrounding the conserved Asp-Glu catalytic dyad are likely to drive the specificity of WbaP to UDP-Gal.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from the structural differences.

claim: The liponanoparticle-based approach for purification of S. enterica WbaP provides a convenient way to add contrast to vitrified particles in CryoEM by way of additional lipid and SMA mass.
source: The liponanoparticle-based approach for purification of S. enterica WbaP provides a convenient way to add contrast to vitrified particles in CryoEM by way of additional lipid and SMA mass, similar to the rationale for utilization of nanobody fusion strategies in the study of other small membrane proteins (Uchański et al., 2021; Wu and Rapoport, 2021).
evidence: This is an inference based on the successful use of SMALP in this study and citations to prior research.

claim: Future efforts to improve the overall resolution of Lg-PGT CryoEM reconstructions may benefit from a combination of liponanoparticle and nanobody approaches.
source: Future efforts to improve the overall resolution of Lg-PGT CryoEM reconstructions may benefit from a combination of these approaches whereby mass from a liponanoparticle facilitates particle identification and picking, while bound nanobody or nanobody complexes/fusions reduce structural motion of the bound Lg-PGT and add distinct features to aid in masking and 3D refinement.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research directions.
